summary.headline: Sasken Q2 FY27 revenue rose 25.6% YoY to Rs.321 Cr with EBITDA margin up 330 bps QoQ to 12.9%, driven by software services.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue was Rs.321 Cr, up 25.6% YoY but down 5.4% QoQ, taking H1 revenue to Rs.660 Cr (+24.8%). Software services drove growth at Rs.252 Cr (+34% YoY, +14.6% QoQ), while product solutions fell 42% QoQ to Rs.69 Cr on memory availability and component pricing pressures. Margins improved: gross margin 26.8%, EBITDA margin 12.9%, EBIT margin 8.9%, and PAT Rs.26 Cr (8% margin). TCV signed was $47 Mn, with $25 Mn new bookings, and management said the 60x4x3 target is delayed by about 12 months.

financial_highlights.change: +~490 bps QoQ; H1 24.3% vs 19.3% prior year

financial_highlights.value: $47 Mn ($25 Mn new bookings, rest renewals)

segments.name: Software services
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs.252 Cr (+34% YoY, +14.6% QoQ) with gross margin 32.2%, up 160 bps QoQ. Order book of about $33 Mn in the $47 Mn TCV. Management guides to single-digit growth on a sustained basis going forward.

segments.name: Product solutions (incl. Sasken Silicon, Borqs)
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs.69 Cr (-42% QoQ) with gross margin 7% (5.9% in Q1), helped by silicon ramp. Run-rate about $7-8 Mn per quarter; management targets $12-14 Mn per quarter for 10-12% EBITDA margin. Order book about $14 Mn.

guidance_outlook: Management said software services growth will moderate to above industry average, with single-digit growth on a sustained basis for the foreseeable future.
About 90-95% of H2 service revenue is already tied up, per management, and it is fairly confident of achieving annual numbers.
The 60x4x3 target (about $240 Mn revenue) is delayed by about 12 months; pursued through organic and inorganic routes.
Product solutions at about $60 Mn annual run-rate should deliver about 10% EBITDA margin, per management.
No formal consolidated growth guidance; management expects continued momentum in top line and margins.
Management sees 90-95% of FY27 memory requirement secured, supporting the next two quarters.
capex_capacity: Product solutions run-rate about $7-8 Mn per quarter; scaling to $12-14 Mn per quarter targeted for 10-12% EBITDA margin.
Headcount grew 7% QoQ; LTM attrition 9.3%; utilization improved to 86%.
Juniper Alta device developed end-to-end and shipped within 18 months.
Manufacturing is outsourced to third-party EMS providers for the product business.
Inventory rose sharply, mainly memory and other components, backed by firm customer orders according to management.
demand_pricing: Four new logos added in Q2; active customers at 101.
Top 5 customers contributed 49% of revenue (56% in Q1); top 10 at 63%. Top 5 revenue was Rs.157 Cr in Q2 vs Rs.187 Cr in Q4 FY26, per an analyst's figures.
Wins include a multiyear telematics program with a European automotive group (3-4 years), cockpit and ADAS work for a European OEM, and an Indian EV company engagement.
Memory: 90-95% of FY27 requirement secured; shifted from DDR5 to DDR4 and lower memory configurations to manage cost.
Order book is spread across semiconductors, automotive, devices, communications and ODM, per management; no vertical split disclosed.
Borqs hardware: building North American sales; RFPs from US telecom carriers; Best Buy re-won.

qa_highlights.question: How will product solutions perform given memory shortage, and what growth is expected in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Hareesh Ramanna said 90-95% of FY27 memory is secured through direct suppliers, customers and the open market, and configuration changes (DDR5 to DDR4) support order sizes.

qa_highlights.question: Why did services revenue rise sharply, and will it continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajiv Mody said growth came from ramp-ups on multiple programs and bench redeployment; going forward, management expects single-digit growth on a sustained basis.

qa_highlights.question: Top 5 and top 10 customer share is falling; how will revenue from large customers grow?
qa_highlights.answer: Priyaranjan said the 60x4x3 strategy aims to broad-base customers; he said all services customers grew in the quarter, and the top 5 names are unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: What sustainable margins should be expected for software services and product solutions?
qa_highlights.answer: Priyaranjan said services margins are improving steadily; product margins are lumpy and should be judged annually. Mody said $60 Mn run-rate should deliver about 10% EBITDA margin, and $12-14 Mn per quarter gives 10-12%.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the currency gain is structural?
qa_highlights.answer: Priyaranjan said exchange rate contributed about 0.5% of margin improvement QoQ; the rest came from utilization, bench cost cuts and operating leverage.

qa_highlights.question: What is the product business and how much of the order book is services vs product?
qa_highlights.answer: Hareesh Ramanna described turnkey concept-to-support delivery through third-party EMS. Priyaranjan said about $33 Mn of the $47 Mn order book is services, with the rest product solutions.

qa_highlights.question: When will the European telematics, cockpit and ADAS wins generate revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Mody said revenue recognition began in Q2 with further expansion from Q3; Yogesh Rathi said full ramp-up was achieved by October 1, 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Will 60x4x3 be achieved, and how much of H2 service revenue is covered?
qa_highlights.answer: Mody said the 240 Mn revenue goal may slip about 12 months, and that about 90-95% of H2 revenue is tied up. Customer-level numbers were not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the growth path for Sasken Silicon and royalty revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Anup Savla said silicon revenue is split roughly equally between consulting and IP licensing, and no royalties are yet earned; royalties are expected in coming years. Silicon revenue was not disclosed separately.

risks_watch: Product solutions volatility from memory and component supply and pricing; inventory build of memory and components.
Top 5 customer concentration (49%) and the 60x4x3 target now delayed about 12 months.
Sequential revenue decline (-5.4% QoQ) and reliance on services growth moderating to single digits.
Automotive demand environment, which management described as a transition with geopolitical and technology pressures.
Exchange rate tailwind (about 0.5% of QoQ margin gain) may not be sustained.
No royalty revenue yet from Sasken Silicon IP; timing remains multiyear.
summary.management_tone: Confident on margins and order momentum, but guarded on product solutions, where management said stability needs more time. It was evasive on vertical splits, customer-level data and silicon revenue, and it acknowledged the 60x4x3 target has slipped about 12 months.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin rose 330 bps QoQ to 12.9% and software services gross margin is 32.2% (+160 bps QoQ), with management saying services margins are improving steadily; product solutions need $12-14 Mn per quarter (vs $7-8 Mn run-rate) to reach 10-12% EBITDA, and the FX tailwind is only ~0.5% of the QoQ gain.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Software services revenue rose 14.6% QoQ to Rs.252 Cr and about 90-95% of H2 services revenue is tied up, but management guides to only single-digit sustained growth and the $33 Mn services order book is modest against that.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is 86% (up), which would normally point to capex, but the call gave no capex or capacity plan; the product business is outsourced to EMS partners and headcount grew 7% QoQ, so the capacity need is being met without capex.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management guides services to single-digit sustained growth and has pushed the 60x4x3 ($240 Mn) target out by about 12 months, so no upgrade is signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Product solutions fell 42% QoQ to Rs.69 Cr on memory and component pressure, top 5 customers fell to 49% of revenue from 56% in Q1, and the 60x4x3 target was already cut by about 12 months.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Juniper Alta was shipped within 18 months and Borqs is building North American sales with US telecom RFPs, but no specific new launch date was given.

rows.label: Borqs hardware North America push
rows.why: Borqs is building North American sales with RFPs from US telecom carriers and a Best Buy re-win, but no revenue figure was given.

rows.label: European automotive telematics, cockpit and ADAS ramp
rows.why: Revenue recognition began in Q2 with expansion from Q3, and full ramp-up was reached by October 1, 2026; the multiyear telematics programme runs 3-4 years.

rows.label: Sasken Silicon royalty revenue
rows.why: No royalties are earned yet and management expects them only in coming years, with silicon revenue not disclosed separately.
